note: Provenance addendum for the supplementary current-main delta relock. It records the commit range between the first relock target and the current main, the call-site linkage and the review evidence behind the second-layer findings. It carries NO severity, production state, score or priority of its own: those live only in docs/security/s1-risk-register.json, and this document shows them as a read-only projection that the checker recomputes. The first-layer document is preserved as a sealed layer and is not rewritten. Every derived section is recomputed from git, from the S0 inventory and from the canonical register by scripts/security/s1/relock-delta-check.mjs; nothing derived is trusted. Contains no secret, no request data, no absolute path and no timestamp.

attribution.historicalBaseline: The S0/S1 audit was performed in full on the original frozen source. Nothing in the historical documents was re-audited against either relock target; the historical snapshot in the canonical register is pinned and recomputed.
attribution.currentMainDelta: Everything main gained between the first relock target and the second relock target. This layer audits that range only, on the tree that integrates the final commit of the first relock lane into the second target. The range from the original frozen source to the first target belongs to the first layer and is not re-opened here.
attribution.reconciledTree: The result of merging the final commit of the first relock lane into the second target, plus the unstaged assurance changes of this layer. The S0 inventory, its adjudications and the canonical register were regenerated on this tree; the first-layer document stays bound to its own sealed tree.

sourceBehavior.summary: The audit console page now renders the Executive Centre link, which calls the executive gate; the test of whether the database client is present is unchanged.

The create handler accepts an optional explicit slug: when it is supplied the handler probes the organization once and answers a conflict for a taken slug, otherwise the derived-slug path is unchanged; the unavailable answer for a missing client is unchanged.
The author sitemap list now skips an author whose handle carries the retired company identity; the empty answer for a missing client is unchanged.
The accessor now also requires the party delegate, so a client generated without it makes every priority source unavailable and not only the customer source.

The generating pass now also freezes the next day's priority list in a read-consistent transaction and stores it in a separate column; a list that cannot be read leaves the report without one, and the answer for a missing client is unchanged.

findings.title: The frozen priority list is shown to the archive reader at the nightly worker's full breadth
findings.summary: The nightly pass now freezes a ranked priority list into a separate column of the report row. The list is built under the same synthetic OWNER scope as the snapshot, which since this range also holds the customers axis, so it names customers, work items and open alerts of every active site. The archive reads the column back unchanged and the detail page renders it without consulting the reader's authority or site list, exactly as it renders the snapshot. This widens the surface of the first-layer finding on the detail page: a reader who may open the archive but holds none of the axes behind a source can read that source's items, including customer names.
findings.callsiteRelation: getReport is the read that now also returns the frozen priority list to the detail page; its null branch is unchanged.

evidence.anchor: authority: { operations: true, financial: true, industrial: true, customers: true },
evidence.note: The report is produced under a synthetic OWNER scope that now also holds the customers axis.
The priority list is computed in the generating pass from that scope.

evidence.anchor: prioritySnapshot: priorities as unknown as Record<string, unknown> | null,
evidence.note: The list is stored in its own column of the report row.

The stored list is rendered as it was stored.

evidence.anchor: select: { id: true, displayName: true, nextActionAt: true, createdAt: true },
evidence.note: A follow-up item carries the customer's display name.
The customers axis is a separate permission, so a stored list can be wider than what a reader holds.
A reader is admitted by any one axis, and the page never asks which axis a stored section was built with.

findings.title: Customer names are copied into a frozen report column that no erasure, export or retention path covers
findings.summary: A follow-up item in the frozen priority list carries the customer's display name, read from the customer record at the moment of the pass and stored as JSON in the report row. The report row is removed only when the organization is deleted, and the platform's closed erasure, export and processing registries do not name the report table or the new column. A customer name therefore stays in every earlier report whatever later happens to the customer record. Which retention the owner requires for a frozen list that names customers is the same undecided question as for the user names in the frozen snapshot.

evidence.note: The frozen list is an unbounded JSON column on the report row.
The column is added without a retention or expiry rule.

findings.title: The executive performance test treats any URL with a local or test marker as a disposable database and writes into the first organization it finds
findings.summary: The performance suite decides that a target is disposable with a regular expression that is not anchored, applied to the whole URL string, so a local port forwarded to a real database, or a marker placed in a query parameter or a user name, passes. It then seeds the first organization of that database by identifier with thousands of customers and has no teardown: its only cleanup closes the connection. Nothing in the repository removes the rows or proves that they are gone. The suite is off by default and runs only through a dedicated script, so this is an operator hazard and not a path a request can reach.

evidence.note: The script that runs the suite names the dedicated configuration and nothing that limits the target.
The only guard is a substring test over the whole URL.

evidence.anchor: const org = await prisma.organization.findFirst({ select: { id: true }, orderBy: { id: "asc" } });
evidence.note: The first organization of the target database receives the seeded customers.
The seeding writes the configured number of customers into that organization.
No statement in the suite removes a row, so nothing the run wrote is cleaned up.
A dedicated configuration selects only the suite that writes.
The ordinary configuration excludes the suite, which is the control that keeps it out of a normal run.

supersessions.statement: The identifier and the fingerprint did not change. The call site was re-examined anyway: the only change in the file is the customers axis in the synthetic scope, and the pass still stops with a failed organization when the client is absent, so the terminal behaviour and the retry trace are as adjudicated.

The first-layer document and its report are preserved. They stay bound to the tree of the final commit of the first relock lane, through the reconciled tree commit they now name, so a later tree cannot move their figures.

The call-site identifiers in the first-layer document name positions in the sealed tree. Where the current tree moved a call site, the current identifier appears in the getPrisma section of this document together with the identifier it replaced.

Every call-site count in those documents describes the original frozen source. The counts for the integrated tree are in the getPrisma section of this document and in docs/security/s0-getprisma-callsite-inventory.json.

openItems.statement: Every finding is code-confirmed on the second target tree. None was exercised at run time and no production request was made.

The summary cache is invalidated only by customer writes. A change to projects, tasks, work orders, approvals, alerts or sites reaches a cached summary only through its time limit, and without Redis the generation counter is per process. The number of production replicas was not observed.

The backup freshness gate parses its verification record with text tools and trusts the producer of that record: it is a freshness check and not tamper evidence. The workflow does not define the maximum-age variable, so the script default applies.

The zero-width class used by the stale-process-text detector omits U+200E and U+200F, while the invisible-character fold used elsewhere in the same checker removes them. A phrase interleaved with those two marks is not matched by the detector. The two marks are recorded here as a residual limitation of the checker; the checker was not changed for it.
The retired-identity test matches the three name parts in order. A look-alike spelling is not matched, and the article pages that list a retired author were not part of this range.

The S0 and S1 checkers are not wired into any workflow or package script, so no pull-request check runs them, and an absent check is not evidence of a pass. Read-only queries of the repository host at the time of this relock showed no classic branch protection on main and an active ruleset that requires a pull request with zero approvals and one status check named Validate; none of the security checkers is that check. Wiring them is a separate change and was not made here.

R-65 and R-72 were re-derived for the surface the second layer added, factor by factor, in a structured revision of each risk. No factor moves, so their scores and severities are reproduced by arithmetic and the first relock's snapshot is unchanged. The customers axis widens the stored priority list of R-65 and adds no organization role that the industrial axis did not already admit.

The name heuristic that lists auth, session, middleware, proxy and nginx paths also matches the article author page, so the derived list of such paths holds one entry that is not an authentication surface.
A host-specific path appears in the historical edge document as provenance and in the selftest fixtures as synthetic input. Neither is personal data or a live location, and neither was changed.

The fix for the performance suite's database guard (R-74) is a change to a test file that is part of the range under review. It is recorded here and in the register and is left for a separate, separately authorized change; this review changes no file of the product.
